name: Die Kreuzen
label: Touch and Go
lede: Die Kreuzen were one of the fastest hardcore bands in the Midwest, then slowed down on purpose, and somebody wrote "You suck now" on their van for it.

eras.title: The Stellas leave Rockford
eras.text: Two friends from Rockford, Illinois moved up to Milwaukee and found a bassist and a drummer who wanted to play as fast as they did. Milwaukee's underground was blue-collar and mixed up with art and theater, and Die Kreuzen were taking their cues from the new hardcore records coming out of California.

years.src: Wikipedia: Die Kreuzen · Perfect Sound Forever · Echoes and Dust
years.h: Two Rockford kids form a Milwaukee band named from a German Bible
years.p: Dan Kubinski and Brian Egeness, playing as the Stellas, add Keith Brammer on bass and his friend Erik Tunison on drums. The name is ungrammatical German for "the crosses".
years.xp:
Their first recordings, "Pain" and "Hate Me", went out on the Charred Remains compilation tape on the local Version Sound label in 1981.

Brammer remembers the Milwaukee scene as "more blue-collar than it has become", with an underground that "included visual arts and theater as well as music."

years.src: Trouser Press · Voyd Productions · Wikipedia: Die Kreuzen
years.h: Cows and Beer: six songs in under seven minutes
years.p: The debut 7-inch, on Version Sound, is the only Die Kreuzen record Touch and Go didn't release. "Hate Me", "Pain" and "In School" come back on the first album.

years.cap: Kubinski and Brammer on stage, c. 1983
years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Echoes and Dust
yt: Live at Centro American Social Club, Milwaukee, March 18, 1983
years.h: Corey Rusk signs them to Touch and Go without a contract
years.p: Rusk met the band on the road with his own group, the [[Necros|a8971728-0985-4b30-a209-142784e7c3b8]]. They never signed anything and worked on trust.
years.xp: "Corey's attitude was (and still is) that he only releases things that he likes," Brammer told Perfect Sound Forever. Decades on he called Rusk "the most honest, straightforward person I have ever met, and a big part of why we were able to do as much as we did."

yt: Die Kreuzen, live on public access TV, 1983
years.h: Public access TV catches the hardcore Die Kreuzen in 1983
years.p: The four-piece at full speed on local television, a year before the first album.

eras.title: Twenty-one songs, then the turn
eras.text: The first album was 21 songs of fast, sharply cut hardcore. Two years later they slowed down, stretched out and let Egeness loose, and some of their own fans took it personally.

yt: Live at the Balboa Theater, Los Angeles, November 1985
years.h: Twenty-one songs in 29 minutes, cut in six days in Detroit
years.p: Rusk produced the debut himself at Multi-Track Studios, April 2 to 7. Trouser Press heard riffs that were "uncommonly well-articulated".
years.xp: It closes with "All White", the longest song on the record at 3:38. The album is usually counted as their last pure hardcore record before the change.

yt: Live at the Hoosier Ballroom, Indiana, 1986
years.h: October File trades speed for odd time signatures and creepy effects
years.p: Fourteen slower, more conceptual songs, with Egeness finally free to play long, dizzy leads.
years.xp: Decibel compared the jump from the first album to the change between the first two [[Meat Puppets|3df040ee-2b8b-446b-937a-3f86f4b2cabf]] records, and put the band's restlessness alongside SST bands like [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]] and the [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]].

years.h: Tunison comes back to the van after a show to find a message on it
years.p: Someone had scrawled it on the side of the band's van. Kubinski says he still gets letters from fans, decades later, who felt October File betrayed them.

years.h: Steve Albini interviews the band for Forced Exposure
years.p: [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]'s piece, "Die Kreuzen: Putting With Potatoes", runs in issue No. 10 of the Boston fanzine.

years.h: The New York Times files them next to Black Sabbath
years.p: Robert Palmer calls Die Kreuzen one of the new bands "recasting the legacy of 70's Gothic-metal (Black Sabbath, etc.) for this modern age."

eras.title: Horns, piano and Butch Vig
eras.text: Butch Vig became their producer before anyone outside Wisconsin knew his name. The records got bigger, quieter in places and stranger, and the band toured the US about ten times in vans and on floors.

years.h: Vig brings in a sax and a trumpet for Century Days
years.p: Recorded from December 1987 to January 1988 at Breezeway in Waukesha, with Peter Balistrieri on saxophones and Tim Cole on trumpet. The CD adds John Carpenter's "Halloween".
years.xp: Egeness plays piano too, and some songs are close to acoustic. Trouser Press called it "an album of impressive dynamic range and sonic control"; the Washington Post heard more early-'70s metal than hardcore. Wikipedia puts its sales at about 10,000 copies in its first three years.

years.cap: Erik Tunison on drums at Isola nel Kantiere, Bologna, December 1989
years.h: Gone Away: two new songs and five live ones
years.p: A 12-inch with one side at 45 and one at 33, the live tracks taped in January 1989.

years.cap: Die Kreuzen at Isola nel Kantiere, Bologna, December 1989
years.h: Kubinski and Egeness moonlight as Chick Treat, a Cheap Trick tribute
years.p: Brammer also joins the Chicago band Wreck that year while staying in Die Kreuzen.

q: They could have been as massive as Jane's Addiction
years.h: Cement, cut with Vig at Smart Studios in Madison
years.p: The last album, recorded in summer 1991, the year Vig's [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] record came out. A hidden acoustic "Gone Away" sits at the end.
years.xp:
The songs grew out of jams, with Kubinski writing the words. The Washington Post: "Less monomaniacal than previously but no less urgent."

Vig has said they just missed the window: "They could have been as massive as Jane's Addiction."

eras.title: Egeness leaves, the others keep going
eras.text: Ten years in, the four wanted different things. Egeness left in spring 1992 and the rest scattered into a run of Milwaukee bands.

years.src: Wikipedia: Die Kreuzen · Perfect Sound Forever
years.h: Brian Egeness leaves, and Die Kreuzen stops
years.p: Brammer later put the end down to the members wanting different directions. Kubinski, Brammer and Tunison start Chainfall with guitarist Charles Jordan of S.O.D.A. and Nerve Twins.
years.xp: Brammer on why the records changed so much: "we would automatically reject anything that sounded like something we had done before."

years.h: Tunison drums on Killdozer's farewell tour
years.p: Kubinski and Tunison also play in Fuckface, Brammer in the Carnival Strippers, and all three in the industrial group Boy Dirt Car. Egeness later scores films.

eras.title: The tribute, the dinosaur suit and the book
eras.text: Other bands kept the records alive first. Then Milwaukee put Die Kreuzen in its hall of fame, the band came back for a sold-out night at Turner Hall, and the fan who stage-dived that night wrote their oral history.

q: there was a point there when Die Kreuzen were the best band in the USA
years.h: Napalm Death, Mike Watt and Voivod line up for a tribute album
years.p: Lean Into It: A Tribute to Die Kreuzen also has Season to Risk and Vic Bondi, with liner notes by [[Thurston Moore|8ba48525-d922-42ee-9775-97b7b8f9712e]].

yt: Die Kreuzen accepting WAMI Hall of Fame Award, Milwaukee, 2011
years.h: The Wisconsin Area Music Industry Hall of Fame inducts them
years.p: In the speech they pass the spotlight on, naming IfIHadAHiFi, Northless, the Zebras and Zola Jesus as artists who deserve it.

years.cap: Kubinski and Brammer at Turner Hall, Milwaukee, May 2012
years.src: There's Something Hard in There · Wikipedia: Die Kreuzen
yt: Die Kreuzen, In School (reunion show, May 26, 2012)
years.h: Twenty years on, a sold-out reunion at Turner Hall
years.p: The Lest We Forget benefit in Milwaukee, with Jay Tiller on guitar in place of Egeness. The 11-song set runs from "In School" to "Man in the Trees".
years.xp: The house was packed with old faces and young punks. Sahan Jayasuriya, reviewing it, ranked it with My Bloody Valentine's 2008 return among the best reunion sets he'd seen, and stage-dived in a dinosaur suit.

years.h: After Roadburn in Tilburg, Turner Hall again with an unrecorded song
years.p: The band plays the Dutch festival in April, then returns to Milwaukee with "Continuous Dogs" in a set that also has "All White" and "Elizabeth".

years.src: Wikipedia: Die Kreuzen · Echoes and Dust
yt: Rock Doc: Die Kreuzen, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel
years.h: Sahan Jayasuriya's Don't Say Please tells the story in their words
years.p: Feral House publishes the oral history, with Thurston Moore, Steve Albini, Neko Case, Butch Vig and [[Lou Barlow|6523f86d-11d3-489e-81f6-6cbe08c367de]] among the voices.
years.xp: Kubinski now fronts the Crosses, who play the first album in full and most of October File. Brammer, asked about playing again: "I've learned to never say never."
